clue.text: Very small snaps or comical pics

indicators.note: to snap is to break apart suddenly, so the letters of the following words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A photographer's tiny prints, whether snapshots or funny pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snaps' looks like a noun for photographs alongside 'pics', but it is the verb telling you to rearrange OR COMICAL PICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Microscopical is an older form of microscopic, describing something so tiny it needs a lens to be seen.

clue.text: Millions on bridge to see King?

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)
an arch is a curved bridging structure, and a bridge may be built as one

explanation.surface: Someone crossing a bridge with millions of others to catch a glimpse of the King.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is one kind of sovereign ruler; the question mark admits a queen would serve as well.

clue.text: Queen, English, sat in patrol-car, endlessly shocked

indicators.note: the English letter is seated inside the jumbled remains of the car word
a shocked arrangement is jolted out of order, so the letters are rearranged
without its end, so the final letter of the hyphenated word goes

explanation.surface: A queen, English, rides in a police car and is appalled by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last R of PATROLCAR; 'shocked' rearranges PATROLCA into CLOPATRA, and 'sat in' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruling Ptolemaic queen of Egypt, a famous female sovereign.

clue.text: Compensates for poor court performance?

definitions.meaning: counterbalances or makes up for something
read as two words, sets of tennis played when a player is off form, an off day on court

explanation.surface: Making amends for a bad showing on the tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into OFF SETS: sets in a tennis match played below par.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset a loss is to counterbalance it with a gain, the ordinary verb meaning of the word.

clue.text: Fake Conservative party on the rise

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word for party is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A sham Tory party gaining in the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rise' turns DO upwards to OD in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, cod means mock or imitation, as in a cod accent or cod philosophy.

clue.text: Biblical writer dismissing a second fortune-teller

indicators.note: sending away, so a letter is removed from the writer's title

parts.note: the Psalmist, traditionally David, wrote the Book of Psalms
S is the abbreviation for a second of time

explanation.surface: A scripture writer brushing aside a rival prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmist reads the lines of a hand to foretell someone's future, a kind of soothsayer.

clue.text: Medium in unconscious state for the shortest interval

indicators.note: the medium letter is placed inside the word for an unconscious state

parts.note: a coma is a state of prolonged unconsciousness
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A spiritualist medium in a trance for only the briefest moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a psychic, which fits 'unconscious state' in the surface; here it is only M.
explanation.definitionFit: In music theory a comma is a minute difference in pitch, the smallest interval normally named.

clue.text: Fielder to want support

parts.note: to long for something is to want it
a leg supports a table or chair

explanation.surface: A fielder who would like some backing from the team.
explanation.walkthrough: Long leg is a cricket fielding position deep behind the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Long leg names a cricket fielding position, and by extension the player standing there.

clue.text: A French Duke unexpectedly freed in a starved condition

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: things happening unexpectedly come out of their expected order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat, surprisingly released from prison, is half-starved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A French' is a translation step, not a nationality; 'unexpectedly' signals the jumble of the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Underfed means given too little food, which is to be starved or malnourished.

clue.text: Keen fellows put in muscle

indicators.note: the fellows are placed inside the muscle word

parts.note: lat is short for latissimus dorsi, a large back muscle
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Eager chaps get into some muscle-building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like an adjective meaning eager, but here it is the verb to wail.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in mourning, so both words mean to grieve aloud over a death.

clue.text: Supporter favouring Prince

parts.note: pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: A royalist backing the Prince.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is a support that holds something up, physically or figuratively.

clue.text: Blurred pixel TV system is readily understood

indicators.note: a blurred image has its parts smeared out of place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: cable is a television delivery system

explanation.surface: A fuzzy picture on cable television is easy to figure out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something explicable can be explained, so it is comprehensible; 'readily' stretches it slightly.

clue.text: Dandy having some veg served with chicken?

parts.note: a pea is one vegetable
a cock is a male chicken; the question mark flags it as an example

explanation.surface: A fop eating a chicken dinner with vegetables on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: A vain, showy man is called a peacock, after the bird that displays its tail.

clue.text: A little ease after a storm in Russian waters

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount

indicators.note: a storm tosses things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The weather calms a bit once a storm passes over Russian seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a storm' reads like a time phrase, but it tells you to toss the letters of 'ease'.
explanation.definitionFit: The White Sea is an inlet of the Barents Sea off northwest Russia.

clue.text: Island also home to hunter's target

indicators.note: a place home to something contains it, so the second word goes inside the first

parts.note: too means also
a bag is the game a hunter aims to shoot

explanation.surface: An island that also has game worth hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island, part of the nation of Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: UK national penning original document: Energy from Sulphur

indicators.note: to pen in is to enclose, so the document goes inside the national

parts.note: a Briton is a citizen of Britain
MS, manuscript, is a handwritten original
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A British author writing a first draft on sulphur as an energy source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Brimstone is the archaic name for sulphur, as in hellfire and brimstone.

clue.text: Difficult to get rid of last stupid bug

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for difficult is discarded

parts.note: hard means difficult
an ass is a stupid person

explanation.surface: A daft insect that is hard to get rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' looks like an insect but is the verb to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to annoy or pester them persistently, the same as to badger.

clue.text: Not supporting benefits in lifting tax cut

indicators.note: the benefits go inside the remaining letters
in a down entry, lifting reads the shortened word upwards
cut short, so the last letter of tax goes

parts.note: gains are benefits

explanation.surface: Opposing tax cuts that would boost welfare benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' and 'lifting' both act on 'tax', leaving AT; 'in' then places the benefits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something means opposing it, the opposite of backing it.

clue.text: My fault being upset about coarse detergent

indicators.note: the reversed exclamation goes around the second word
in a down entry, upset turns the exclamation upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: oops is what you say on making a mistake
ham acting is coarse, overdone performance

explanation.surface: Apologising after knocking over a harsh cleaning product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being upset' turns the exclamation to SPOO; 'about' wraps it round the coarse word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid soap for cleaning hair or carpets, so it is a kind of cleanser.

clue.text: Innovative in exam, consuming one drink

indicators.note: eating up, so the exam word swallows the others

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A creative student having a drink during an oral exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Original work is new and inventive, not copied, so it is fresh and creative.

clue.text: Guts of mechanism in pubs on either side of a road

indicators.note: the pubs word is split to flank the other letters

parts.note: inns are pubs

explanation.surface: The inner workings of a machine housed in pubs that line a road.
explanation.definitionFit: The innards of a machine are its internal working parts, as the guts of an animal are its insides.

clue.text: Russian car retaining edge, turning up as foremost in fleet

indicators.note: in a down entry the assembled letters are read upwards
holding on to, so the car contains the edge

parts.note: the Lada is a Russian make of car
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A Russian car keeping to the verge as it leads a fleet of vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retaining' makes LA(RIM)DA, and 'turning up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The admiral is the highest-ranking naval officer, so the chief of a fleet.

clue.text: Graduate meeting grandmother's family — a hazardous step here?

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
nana's is an informal possessive for grandmother
kin are family

explanation.surface: A graduate meeting their grandmother's relatives, a risky move.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic slapstick slip happens on discarded fruit peel underfoot, so it is where a dangerous step lands.

clue.text: Focus of religious activity almost entirely black

indicators.note: nearly all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: all means entirely, as in all alone
tar is black

explanation.surface: A place of worship painted almost wholly black.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the table at the centre of worship where offerings or communion take place.

clue.text: Identical look thrown out by famous dancer

indicators.note: expelled from, so the look word is removed from the dancer

parts.note: Salome danced the dance of the seven veils for Herod
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A celebrated dancer rejects a lookalike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look' is LO, as in 'lo and behold', removed from SALOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that are the same are indistinguishable, which is the plain meaning of identical.

clue.text: Elected members favoured coming back with agreement

parts.note: the ins are those in office, elected

indicators.note: returning, so the word for favoured is read backwards

parts.note: a pet is a favoured one, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Elected representatives backing a favoured policy in agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ins' is an old term for the party in power.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in step means moving in harmony, so acting in accord with others.

clue.text: Worry about a good deal in sexual activity

indicators.note: around, so the worry word goes round the other

parts.note: to harry is to worry or harass
a lot is a good deal

explanation.surface: Fretting over a great amount of time spent in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlotry is prostitution or promiscuity, an old word for immoral sexual conduct.

clue.text: Man's expression of disapproval cut short

indicators.note: with its tail docked, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a hiss is a sound of disapproval from an audience

explanation.surface: A man's grumble of disapproval interrupted mid-sound.
explanation.definitionFit: His is the possessive pronoun belonging to a male person.

clue.text: Broadcast the stories associated with LOL cat

indicators.note: scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Spreading tales about an internet cat meme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' rearranges THE STORIES with LOL; 'LOL cat' is internet slang for a captioned cat picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoiseshell is a cat with mottled black, orange and cream fur.
